datasource_insert_rows.name: datasource_insert_rows
datasource_insert_rows.description: Insert rows of data into a table in the configured datasource (works for Postgres, BigQuery, Redshift, or MSSQL). Returns a descriptive string confirming insertion success or detailing any errors.

table_name.description: Name of the table to insert data into

data.description: The row(s) to insert. If single_row is true, a single object representing one row; otherwise an array of objects representing multiple rows

single_row.description: Set to true if data is a single row object (it will be wrapped into a one-item list); false if data is already an array of rows. Defaults to false.

datasource_insert_multi.name: datasource_insert_multi
datasource_insert_multi.description: Insert rows into MULTIPLE tables of one datasource atomically, in a single all-or-nothing transaction (any failure rolls back every table). Currently supported for Postgres datasources only. Returns a descriptive string confirming success or detailing any errors.

inserts.description: An array of per-table insert specs. Each item is an object {"table_name": string, "data": row-or-rows, "single_row": boolean}. 'data' is a single row object when single_row is true, otherwise an array of row objects. All tables are written in one transaction, so order parents before children for FK constraints.

datasource_execute_query.name: datasource_execute_query
datasource_execute_query.description: Read data from the configured datasource by running a pre-registered dynamic query (works for Postgres, BigQuery, Redshift, or MSSQL). The SQL lives server-side, so a single query can join and aggregate across several tables. Use this to look up existing records before deciding what to write. Returns JSON mapping each query id defined in the query file to its list of result rows, e.g. {"quotes": [{...}]}; an empty list means no rows matched, which is a valid result and not an error. On failure it returns a descriptive error string instead.

query_id.description: Id of the pre-registered dynamic query to run

params.description: An object of values for the named parameters the query declares, e.g. {"p_wavefront_run_id": "abc-123"}. Every declared parameter must be supplied or the call fails. Values are sent as strings. Pass an empty object for queries that declare no parameters.

filter.description: Optional OData filter expression applied on top of the query, e.g. "status eq 'active' $and amount gt 1000". Supported operators are eq, gt, lt, lte, gte, contains and in, combined with $and / $or. Only works on queries that include a {{filters}} placeholder.

limit.description: Maximum number of rows to return. Defaults to 10. Raise it only when more than a lookup is needed.

offset.description: Number of rows to skip, for paging through a large result set. Defaults to 0.

use_cache.description: Set to true to allow a cached result from the last 2 minutes to be returned. Defaults to false so that a read following a write in the same workflow sees the write.

querying_knowlegebase.name: querying_knowlegebase
querying_knowlegebase.description: Query the knowlegebase using the configured datasource. Returns a descriptive string indicating success or failure with connection details.

kb_id.description: UUID of the configured BigQuery datasource

inference_id.description: UUID of the configured BigQuery datasource

send_email.name: send_email
send_email.description: Send an email to the specified recipient. Returns a descriptive string indicating success or failure of the email delivery process.

email_id.description: Email address of the recipient to whom the message will be sent

trigger_message_processor.name: trigger_message_processor
trigger_message_processor.description: Execute a message processor function. This template gets expanded into individual tools for each message processor.

trigger_api_service.name: trigger_api_service
trigger_api_service.description: Execute an API service. This template gets expanded into individual tools for each API.
